turns.ask: Our online game's login API keeps getting hammered by massive DDoS attacks. Design the full protection layer and the backend service behind it.

ops.text: I'll design a DDoS-hardened login API path: ESA for edge defense, Anti-DDoS Proxy for volumetric scrubbing, ALB with WAF, and backend services.

ops.label: Game players
ops.why: Players calling the login API from game clients.

ops.label: Cloud DNS
ops.why: Resolves the login domain to ESA.

ops.label: ESA
ops.why: Edge caching, bot management and first-line DDoS defense.

ops.label: Anti-DDoS Proxy
ops.why: Scrubs massive L3-L7 DDoS attacks before they reach origin.

ops.label: ALB
ops.why: Distributes scrubbed login traffic across two zones.

ops.label: WAF
ops.why: Blocks OWASP attacks and CC floods on the login endpoint.

ops.label: API Gateway
ops.why: Rate-limits and authenticates login API calls.

ops.label: Login servers
ops.why: Validates credentials and issues game session tokens.

ops.label: Session cache
ops.why: Stores rate-limit counters and active sessions in memory.

ops.label: Accounts DB
ops.why: Persists player accounts and credentials with HA standby.

ops.label: NAT Gateway
ops.why: Gives login servers outbound access for patches and APIs.

ops.label: Logs
ops.why: Centralizes attack logs and login audit trails.
